newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Zaire's Gecamines copper, cobalt output rising.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Gecamines copper, cobalt output rising.

text.p: Production of copper and cobalt from mines controlled by Zaire's state-owned mining concern Gecamines has been rising steadily since all-time lows in the early 1990s, according to recent Gecamines figures.
Gecamines said in a recent document it produced 38,900 tonnes of copper in 1996, 4,000 tonnes of cobalt and 3,159 tonnes of zinc.

Mining analysts say the vast Central African country is one of the richest mineral resource areas in the world but corruption and political chaos has devastated its production of base and precious metals.
Gecamines says copper production plunged from 476,000 tonnes in 1986 to a low of 31,300 in 1994, recovering to 36,100 in 1995 and further in 1996.
Zaire remains the world's biggest producer of cobalt but 1996's production was far short of the 14,518 tonnes produced in 1986.

Gecamines attributed the drop in production to the collapse of the Kamoto mine in 1990, technical problems and delays in development of the open-cast Kolwezi copper mine and delays in the rehabilitation of the concentrator/smelter at Kolwezi.

South Africa's Iscor Ltd said last week it had acquired the right to complete a feasibility study for the rehabilitation of Kamoto with estimated reserves of 66 million tonnes grading 4.4 percent copper and 0.5 percent cobalt.
Kolwezi was shut down after foreign exchange dried up and the mine could not afford spare parts for its machinery.
Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd has put in a bid to mine the leftover tailings at Kolwezi.
In the document, Gecamines also cited production equipment failure and the suspension of foreign investment for the plunge in metal output.
Gecamines said with increased investment in the decaying mining industry, Zaire could lift production significantly by 2000.
It said with investment from 1995 to 2000 of $439 million, copper production could increase to 140,000 tonnes, cobalt to 10,000 tonnes and zinc to 13,000 tonnes.
The huge mineral wealth of Zaire has lured some investors despite political chaos and a rising rebel campaign.
Canada's Consolidated Eurocan Ventures has signed an agreement with Gecamines to acquire a 55 percent interest in the giant Tenke Fungurume copper deposit in Shaba province.
Tenke Fungurume is one of the world's largest undeveloped copper and cobalt deposits with inferred resources of 93 million tonnes at 4.6 percent copper and 0.37 percent cobalt.
The deposit is estimated to contain 4.26 million tonnes of copper and 0.34 million tonnes of cobalt. --Johannesburg newsroom, +27-11 482-1003
